units.title: A Nebraska resident needs a license to drive a motor vehicle on the state’s streets or highways.
A newly arrived resident who holds a valid license from another state must obtain Nebraska licensing within thirty days.
Nebraska’s graduated licensing system introduces driving privileges in stages to limit high-risk situations while teenagers gain experience.
Graduated-license restrictions prohibit using an interactive wireless device while the vehicle is moving.
Everyone in a vehicle driven by a permit holder must use a seat belt.
A school-permit holder may transport only household family members to the school that the holder attends.
For the first six months, a provisional-permit driver may carry at most one non-immediate-family passenger who is younger than nineteen.
The graduated restrictions list school-activity and work travel as exceptions to the midnight-to-six-a.m. limit for provisional-permit drivers.
Breaking a driving restriction can lead to license suspension or revocation.
A driver younger than twenty-one who earns at least six points in a year must complete driver improvement within three months.
The school learner permit lets an eligible student practice driving toward a school permit.
A school learner permit applicant must be at least fourteen and cannot apply before that birthday.
A passenger-car school learner must have an adjacent supervising driver aged at least twenty-one who is licensed in Nebraska or another state.
The school learner permit requires vision and written testing.
A school learner permit lasts for six months after issuance.
A school-permit applicant satisfies the geographic condition by living outside a city of five thousand or more people or attending school outside such a city.
A school-permit driver may travel unsupervised by the nearest direct accessible route between home and the attended school or its activity property for scheduled school purposes.
A school-permit holder may drive at any time when accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least twenty-one.
A school-permit applicant must be at least fourteen years and two months old.
Before applying for a school permit, an applicant must have held a school learner permit or learner permit for at least two months.
One route to a school permit is successful completion of a Nebraska driver-safety course approved by the DMV.
The supervised-practice route to a school permit requires certification of fifty driving hours, signed by a parent, guardian or licensed driver aged at least twenty-one.
The school-permit practice certification must include at least ten hours driven between sunset and sunrise.
For a school-permit applicant, completing a Nebraska DMV-approved driver-safety course waives the written and drive tests.
School-permit applicants using the practice certification still need vision and drive testing.
For a school-permit applicant using practice certification, a valid school learner or learner permit, or one expired no longer than a year, waives the written test.
Every occupant riding with a school-permit driver must be secured by an occupant-protection system.
A school permit expires when its holder reaches sixteen years and three months.
The learner permit permits legal driving practice toward a provisional permit or operator license.
A learner permit may be applied for sixty days before the fifteenth birthday, but cannot be issued until age fifteen.
A first graduated-license wireless-device violation carries a two-hundred-dollar fine and license points.
A seat-belt violation under the graduated restrictions carries a twenty-five-dollar fine.
A graduated-permit passenger restriction violation carries one point on the driving record.
A provisional-permit nighttime-driving violation carries one point on the driving record.
A first under-twenty-one zero-tolerance offense results in the court holding the permit or license for thirty days.
A driver younger than twenty-one with a BAC of at least zero point zero eight is subject to the same DWI laws as an adult driver.
A school learner permit applicant must be eligible for a school permit and satisfy all school-permit criteria.
An applicant who was not old enough for a school learner permit when completing the safety course must present the school’s paper waiver when applying for the school permit.
A passenger-car learner-permit holder needs a licensed driver aged at least twenty-one in the adjacent seat.
The learner-permit written test is waived after issuance of a school learner, school or learner permit that is valid or expired no longer than a year.
The learner permit expires a year after it is issued.
A provisional-permit holder may drive without supervision from six a.m. until midnight.
Unsupervised provisional driving between midnight and six a.m. is limited to trips between home and work or a school activity.
A provisional driver may drive at any time with an accompanying parent, guardian or licensed driver who is at least twenty-one.
A provisional permit cannot be issued before the sixteenth birthday, although application may start sixty days earlier.
Before a provisional-permit application, a school learner, school or learner permit must have been held for at least six months.
A provisional applicant must have fewer than three points accumulated during the six months immediately before applying.

The provisional-permit practice route requires certification of fifty driving hours, including ten between sunset and sunrise, signed by a parent, guardian or licensed driver aged at least twenty-one.
A DMV-approved Nebraska driver-safety course waives the provisional written and drive tests.
A provisional applicant using practice certification needs vision and drive tests, with the written test waived for a learner permit valid or expired no longer than a year.
Every person riding with a provisional-permit driver must use an occupant-protection system.
A provisional permit expires on the holder’s eighteenth birthday.
A Class O license authorizes noncommercial motor vehicles, including mopeds, autocycles, all-terrain vehicles and utility-terrain vehicles, but excludes motorcycles and commercial motor vehicles.
An autocycle cannot be used for the Class O drive test.
The minimum age for an operator license is seventeen.
An applicant below age eighteen qualifies for an operator license after holding a provisional permit for at least twelve months with fewer than three points during the previous twelve months.

An operator applicant younger than eighteen receives written- and drive-test waivers after holding a provisional permit for at least twelve months and accumulating fewer than three points during the previous twelve months.
A provisional-permit holder applying for an operator license between ages eighteen and twenty-one receives a waiver of the written and drive tests.

A first-time operator applicant aged eighteen or older who never held a provisional permit needs vision, written and drive tests, with the written test waived for a learner permit that is valid or expired no more than a year.
For a first-time operator applicant aged at least eighteen, a learner permit valid or expired no longer than a year waives the written test.
Applicants below age eighteen who surrender a valid out-of-state permit or license must meet provisional-permit requirements.
A new resident aged at least eighteen who surrenders a valid out-of-state license needs a vision test, with drive testing left to licensing staff discretion.
A new Nebraska resident aged eighteen or older must take the written test if unable to surrender the out-of-state license or if that license has expired.
